method: Complete reads of three pinned BLAKE3 files with Git blob and SHA256 verification. No hash-vector, cross-ISA or throughput execution in this audit.
findings: Public header declares 64-byte blocks, 1024-byte chunks, 32-byte default output/key and depth54 plus one lazy-merge stack slot. finalize/finalize_seek accept const hasher; API includes keyed and derive-key modes, not just file-content hashing. These are interface declarations, not independently verified implementation guarantees.

x86 dispatch checks CPUID and OSXSAVE/xgetbv state before enabling AVX paths. Single compression favors AVX512VL then SSE41/SSE2; multi-input hashing requires AVX512F plus VL, then AVX2/SSE and reports degrees16/8/4. AArch64 NEON selection is compile-time for hash_many, while single compression falls back portable in this dispatch file.
Feature cache uses C atomics when available, Windows interlocked operations under MSVC, otherwise plain int. Source warns TSAN users to enable atomics; no concurrency bug reproduced here.

xof_many explicitly returns on zero requested blocks before an assembly path that would emit at least one block. Fallback loops compression with increasing output-block counter; Windows/Cygwin bypass the AVX512 many-output assembly branch.

Portable implementation loads words, runs seven schedule rounds, writes little-endian CV/XOF output via helpers, and processes many inputs sequentially with optional counter increment. It assumes full blocks in hash_many; arbitrary-tail handling is delegated to the higher-level hasher, still unread.
limits: No correctness or performance certification of cryptographic implementation or CPU targets.
